On 28.10.2023 at about 00.20hours the petitioner was driving the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA- 52-B-8378 on the left side of NICE Road from Bannerghatta Toll towards Electronic City Toll at moderate speed, carefully and cautiously, observing all the traffic rules, a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-A- 9145 driven by its driver was going in-front of petitioner's Canter at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life, when the said Lorry reached near SNN Raj Apartment,
NICE Road without giving any signal or indicator lights on to the vehicles came in the rear side of the said Lorry, the Lorry driver all of a sudden applied the brakes in the middle of the Road, since it was midnight and also due to focus lights coming from opposite vehicles, the petitioner could not notice whether the Lorry was moving or stopped and inspite of the efforts made made by the petitioner to stop his Canter, his Canter rammed on the rear side of the said Lorry.
Due to impact both vehicles damaged extensively and the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Kaveri Hospital, provided first aid treatment then shifted to BOSS Multi Specialty Hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as an inpatient on 28.10.2023, the petitioner underwent right femur IMIL nailing and external fixation of Tibia with popliteal artery repair and guillotine below knee amputation and discharged on 07.11.2023 with an advice to take complete bed rest continue medicine and took follow up treatment.

So far the petitioner has spent Rs.15,00,000/-
towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges and nourishing food and other incidental expenses.

Due to multiple fractures right leg and below knee guillotine,
amputation, as stated supra, the petitioner became physically handicapped person, cannot stand or walk without support, cannot run or walk, cannot climb stairs, cannot squat or sit with crossed legs,
cannot use Indian Toilet and caused permanent disability.

4. It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, working as Driver under 3rd Respondent's Canter and earning Rs.30,000/- per month and was contributing his entire income for welfare and maintenance of his family.

After the accident due to fractures,
amputation of right leg below knee and permanent disability as stated supra, the petitioner became physically handicapped person and unable to do any physical strain work in future and lost his income permanent for the rest of his life.

The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-A-914 and the Electronic City Traffic Police have registered a case against the driver of the said Lorry in their Cr.No.0332/2023 p/u/Secs.279,
338 of IPC.

17. Before discussing on this point, it is necessary to advert to the observations made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.

The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a Saurabh Alias Saurabh Kumar vs Muthuraj on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116341283/
7 result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

sentences.text: The Court or Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

18. Our Hon'ble High Court has held in a case MFA.811 OF 2015 (MV-I) decided on 18 July, 2019 in between Rajanna @ Raju and another V/s Srinivas and another that "It is necessary to understand the meaning of the expression "permanent disability", which has been elucidated in Rajkumar.

entities.text: Rajanna @ Raju and another V/s Srinivas and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to the Hon'ble Supreme Court, disability refers to any restriction or lack of ability to perform an activity in the manner considered normal for a human being.

Permanent disability refers to the residuary incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body, found existing at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation, after achieving the maximum bodily improvement or recovery which is likely to remain for the remainder life of the injured.
Temporary disability refers to the incapacity or loss of use of some part of the body on account of the injury, which will cease to exist at the end of the period of treatment and recuperation.
Permanent disability can be either partial or total.

Partial permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform all the duties and bodily functions that he could perform before the accident, though he is able to perform some of them and is still able to engage in some gainful activity.
Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.

The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor accidents injuries, are of a much wider range when compared to the physical disabilities which are enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 ("the Disabilities Act",
for short).

entities.text: Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995

sentences.text: But if any of the disabilities enumerated in Section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.

the extent of such permanent disability.

By considering the nature of injuries,

PECUNIARY DAMAGES I.

Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines,
transportation, nourishing food and misc. expenditures.
20. The claimant has contended that he has taken treatment at Kaveri Hospital, provided first aid and thereafter shifted Boss Multi-Speciality Hospital, Bangalore wherein admitted as in inpatient.
Further the Discharge Summaries of petitioner produced at Ex.P15 indicates that, the petitioner was admitted on 28.10.2023 and discharged on 07.11.2023 at Boss Multispeciality Hospital, Bangalore.
The petitioner has produced the medical/cash bill.
On careful perusal of the medical bills marked at Ex.P18, it is appears to Court that there is no repetitive bills, advance bills.
There is no contrary evidence from the respondents.
Hence, I award a sum of Rs.4,93,019/- as compensation to the claimant under the head of treatment and medical expenses.
As supra said, the petitioner has admitted in the above said Hospital as an inpatient for a period of nearly 11 days.
Hence, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.500/-per day for attendant and Rs.500/- for food and nourishment charges, which would comes Rs.11,000/-.
A sum of Rs.11,000/- is awarded under the head of attendant, food and nourishment charges.
(ii) LOSS OF EARNING 21.

Therefore, I award Rs.5,700/- to the claimant under the head of loss of earning during the treatment.

opennyai_summary.facts:
On 28.10.2023 at about 00.20hours the petitioner was driving the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA- 52-B-8378 on the left side of NICE Road from Bannerghatta Toll towards Electronic City Toll at moderate speed, carefully and cautiously, observing all the traffic rules, a Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16-A- 9145 driven by its driver was going in-front of petitioner's Canter at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life, when the said Lorry reached near SNN Raj Apartment,
NICE Road without giving any signal or indicator lights on to the vehicles came in the rear side of the said Lorry, the Lorry driver all of a sudden applied the brakes in the middle of the Road, since it was midnight and also due to focus lights coming from opposite vehicles, the petitioner could not notice whether the Lorry was moving or stopped and inspite of the efforts made made by the petitioner to stop his Canter, his Canter rammed on the rear side of the said Lorry.
Due to impact both vehicles damaged extensively and the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
After the accident due to fractures,
amputation of right leg below knee and permanent disability as stated supra, the petitioner became physically handicapped person and unable to do any physical strain work in future and lost his income permanent for the rest of his life.
Hence, the respondent Nos.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It means that, the petitioner was not so vigilant while driving the vehicle and not maintained the safe distance in between the vehicle.
At the same time, material on record are clearly demonstrated that there was no obstacles in front of the offending vehicle.
It is not the case of the insurer of the offending vehicle that the driver of the offending vehicle has applied the brake or slow down the vehicle in order to avoid obstacles appeared infront of the offending vehicle.
It is very pertinent note herein that the alleged accident was occurred at the midnight.
So, at angle it can't be presumed that at the time of accident, road was busy with vehicles or in other words heavy traffic in the NICE road the relevant point of time.
Unless and until, if there being any obstacles in front of the vehicle or heavy traffic, applying sudden brake does not arose at all.
Hence,
it is appears to Court that, the driver of the offending vehicle and petitioner have not so vigilant while driving their vehicles.
If both drivers have taken minimal care, they could have avoid the accident.
Therefore, the Tribunal holds that the accident caused due to the rash and negligence act of the driver of the offending vehicle and also on the part of the driver of the Canter Lorry/Petitioner.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that, the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a Saurabh Alias Saurabh Kumar vs Muthuraj on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116341283/
7 result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The Court or Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
Permanent disability can be either partial or total.
Partial permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform all the duties and bodily functions that he could perform before the accident, though he is able to perform some of them and is still able to engage in some gainful activity.
Total permanent disability refers to a person's inability to perform any avocation or employment related activities as a result of the accident.
The permanent disabilities that may arise from motor accidents injuries, are of a much wider range when compared to the physical disabilities which are enumerated in the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 ("the Disabilities Act",
for short).
But if any of the disabilities enumerated in Section 2(i) of the Disabilities Act are the result of injuries sustained in a motor accident, they can be permanent disabilities for the purpose of claiming compensation.
This means that the Tribunal should consider and decide with reference to the evidence:
(i) whether the disablement is permanent or temporary;
(ii) if the disablement is permanent, whether it is permanent total disablement or permanent partial disablement;
(iii) if the disablement percentage is expressed with reference to any specific limb,
then the effect of such disablement of the limb on the functioning of the entire body,
that is, the permanent disability suffered by the person."
